lifecyclePhase: post-merge structural audit with accepted repository corrections in implementation
acceptedLocalDecisions: The audit is bound only to merged and pushed main revision 4fc8ba1750524581c281ad97351bf0b1e6e29631; both local main and origin/main resolved to that object at scope capture.

packages/infrastructure owns private Alchemy resources, state-safe contracts, Vercel adapters, and composition over the existing @bundjil/photon management boundary; apps do not consume @bundjil/infrastructure.
Vercel Git remains deployment owner while Alchemy owns only the declared stable configuration, adoption, state, and report-only drift boundaries documented by the repository.
ChannelHandoff and ChannelReplay own webhook-to-Eve acceptance and continuity; the provider-specific Sendblue and Photon modules remain thin composition adapters.
The fifteen complete critical-journey IDs are the repository identities; historical proof and completed plans are trajectory evidence only and grant no standing authority.

Cooper's 2026-08-01 implementation delegation accepts FINDING-001 through FINDING-004, accepts count-free routing from FINDING-006, and requires an evidence-backed preserve or defer decision for optional FINDING-005.
claimedJobs: Route a maintainer from repository guidance to one current architecture, SPEC, execution, runbook, proof, and lifecycle owner.
Read, adopt, plan, converge, observe drift in, and roll back the exact stage-scoped Alchemy/Vercel/Photon infrastructure without confusing source proof with provider actuality.
Accept authenticated Sendblue or Photon ingress once, hand it to Eve with continuity fencing, deliver the resulting provider operation, and retain a bounded rollback/recovery route.
Resolve private @bundjil packages consistently from TypeScript source during workspace development and from built exports at package boundaries.
Run repository-owned quality, authority, control, documentation, verification, and package checks and retain only claim-matched evidence.
acceptedOutcomes: A maintainer can identify one present-tense continuation without loading a completed plan or stale task ledger as current policy.
The repository source exposes stage-isolated infrastructure plans, sequential resource composition, observe-first provider adapters, explicit rollback identity, and no implicit deployment ownership.
The Channel route returns 202 only after Eve send acceptance and intended-session continuity convergence; uncertain work remains retryable or quarantined without blind replay.
Each public package concept has one semantic Schema owner and one deliberate export path under the @bundjil/source, types, and default conditions.
Local checks prove only the source and fixture claims they execute; provider, deployment, delivery, and Production claims remain outside this audit.
proofBoundaries: Git-object inventory and diff inspection prove only the exact tracked source at the target revision.
Schema, type, memory-layer, and test inspection prove repository contracts and fixture intent, not a hosted runtime.
Runbook and authority inspection proves repository-owned procedure and gating text, not current authorization or external state.
Historical packets and completed plans establish trajectory and dated provenance only.
The structured audit validator proves artifact shape and accepted-finding crosswalk completeness only.
Repository verification commands require the target worktree's dependencies; failure to resolve a dependency is a local verification limitation, not proof of a source defect.

authority.approvalReceipt: User delegation dated 2026-08-01 permits the accepted repository corrections in an isolated worktree and explicitly excludes all external or provider mutation.

exclusions: Provider reality, credentials, dashboards, billing, webhooks, deployments, messages, external logs, and current Production or Preview state.
Implementation, refactoring, file moves, provider changes, deployment, publication, messaging, commit, push, merge, or finding acceptance.
Ignored and generated node_modules, dist, .turbo, .vercel, tmp, caches, credential files, and local proof artifacts.
Exhaustive deep reading of completed plans and retained proof; those paths were inventoried and only directly relevant trajectory evidence was deep-read.
Mutable upstream documentation or provider claims not already present as repository evidence at the target revision.
stopConditions: Stop finding analysis if HEAD, local main, or origin/main no longer resolves to the supplied target revision.
Stop before changing any source, configuration, provider, deployment, documentation owner, plan, task ledger, or lifecycle route outside the four audit artifacts.
Stop before accepting a finding or producing implementation tasks until Cooper records a decision.
Stop any repository verification that would require installing dependencies or otherwise creating files beyond the four permitted audit artifacts.
Stop any external access or operation because the audit has no provider authority.
limitations: The audit is a static repository review plus repository-owned local checks; it cannot establish external actuality.

The target worktree has no node_modules directory, so Bun checks that import workspace dependencies cannot run without a disallowed dependency-state mutation; this is recorded as unverified rather than treated as a source failure.
Git path inventories establish presence and accounting, not semantic correctness; risk-based deep reads and representative jobs provide the semantic evidence.
Historical evidence was sampled only where it bears directly on current ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, or proof claims.
Line references bind to the exact target revision and will drift after later edits.
nonClaims: No provider, deployment, runtime, message, delivery, billing, secret, Production, Preview, GitHub setting, or external workflow state was read or changed.
No finding is accepted, scheduled, implemented, verified in production, or authorized for implementation.
A green schema validator would prove only artifact conformance, not agreement with the findings.
Preserve findings do not assert that every uninspected line is defect-free.
The audit does not reuse preceding terminal audits as proof of the final merged target.
